new_scholarship.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program funds citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience to pursue a master's degree in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, it offers scholarships for 44 participating master's programs in 24 universities across the United States, Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan, in areas including economic policy management, tax policy and infrastructure management. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.

programme_detail_official.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program is open to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts who are applying to a master's degree program in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, JJ/WBGSP offers scholarships for 44 Participating Master's Programs in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan in key areas of development, including economic policy management, tax policy, and infrastructure management. Applicants who are not admitted to one of these 44 programmes are not eligible to apply in 2027. research_notes.logo: Scanned the awarding body's own JJ/WBGSP page for /logo|brand/i assets. Three candidates appeared: an IMF event logo at /content/dam/sites/service/header/img/am/am-en-logo.svg whose alt text is literally 'IMF World Bank Group Thailand 2026 Logo' (rejected: that is an IMF event mark, not the World Bank's own logo), a generic social-share JPEG (rejected: not a logo), and the site header logo https://www.worldbank.org/content/dam/sites/edge/wbglogo-topnav-eng.svg with alt text 'World Bank Logo'. I probed the header logo with a direct request: HTTP 200, content-type image/svg+xml, 10588 bytes. Because SVG blobs cannot be decoded by createImageBitmap, I rendered it through an Image element to a 220x44 canvas and sampled every opaque pixel: 88.2% dark, 11.8% light, confirming a dark navy #002F54 mark and not a white-on-transparent wordmark. I also probed the stored image /content/dam/wbr-redesign/logos/wbg-favicon.png, which returns HTTP 200 image/png but is only a favicon, and /content/dam/sites/edge/wbglogo-english.svg, which returned HTTP 404 text/html and was rejected.

new_scholarship.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. Applicants must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant during the time of application or be able to prove they will receive one during their term abroad. The programme has funded American students to study and intern abroad in more than 170 countries, with recipients from all 50 U.S. states and D.C.
